summary: Gemini's corrected Phase A report is schema-valid and substantively compatible across enterprise information architecture, architecture, clinical authority, privacy, accessibility, performance, scope, and visual-system direction. One narrow explicit human brand constraint remains: the blueprint specifies diminishing user-facing 'Sandbox' and 'Demo' labels. Preserve the design and replace only that presentation language before exact-digest approval.
review_scope: Compatibility only. Do not substitute Codex aesthetic preferences for Gemini design authority.

required_changes.description: Remove diminishing user-facing framing from the blueprint: do not label OncoReady or its ordinary surfaces Prototype, Demo, Dummy, Mock, or Toy. Replace 'Enter Sandbox' with 'Explore Workspace', 'Sandbox Entry' with 'Workspace Access', 'Reset Demo' with 'Reset Workspace', and 'Local demo' tooltips with neutral read-only explanations. Replace repeated 'Synthetic Data'/'Simulated Event' badges with one discreet professional 'Training environment' indicator plus contextual 'Illustrative records' or 'Mapping preview' language only where material. Internal engineering documentation may still use demo/synthetic terminology. Preserve truthful non-production and no-live-integration boundaries without making the application look unfinished.

notes_for_gemini: Do not redesign the approved direction and do not begin Phase B. Make only the professional product-language correction, update the report if its summaries reference the changed labels, validate, commit, and stop for exact-digest approval.
Keep truthful boundaries subtle: a normal enterprise environment indicator and contextual mapping/status language are enough; do not cover every screen or record with disclaimers.
